description: The floor each clause has to clear to count as meeting what the model templates ask for. Each rule is a list of field checks that must all pass. Change the floor by pull request, with a reason.

community_fund.label: Community fund
community_fund.asks: A fund that scales with the project, with a community seat on the body that spends it

strongest.why: $30 per square foot of approved data center, so the fund scales with what actually gets built instead of being a flat headline number.

clawbacks.label: Clawbacks
clawbacks.asks: Incentives come back if the facility stops operating, not only if a jobs number is missed

strongest.why: Liquidated damages of $2,000 per job short of a 25, 50, then 100 job ladder for 20 years, plus $15,000 for every $100,000 of tax revenue missed. Money, per unit missed, not an all-or-nothing default.

decommissioning.label: Decommissioning
decommissioning.asks: A bond, escrow, or letter of credit that pays for teardown and site restoration if the operator walks

strongest.why: No deal on record posts a bond. The closest is the neighboring town of Marana, which conditioned its approval of the same developer on removing all hardware and securing the property if the use stops.

grid_costs.label: Grid costs
grid_costs.asks: The operator pays for its own interconnection and carries a minimum bill that survives it leaving

strongest.why: Billing demand of at least 85 percent of peak for a twelve year term, an exit fee of 36 months of minimum charges, and collateral of half the total minimum charges unless the customer is investment grade.

water.label: Water
water.asks: A stated cap or closed-loop cooling, plus public reporting

strongest.why: A hard cap of 20,000 gallons a day per campus written into the agreement, against a prior industrial user on the same site that drew 100,000 to 125,000.

noise.label: Noise
noise.asks: A numeric limit measured at the nearest residence or property line

strongest.why: 55 dBA at the residential lot line, a study before the first site plan and again within six months of every occupancy permit, mitigation within 60 days of an exceedance, all certified by an acoustical engineer.

jobs.label: Jobs
jobs.asks: Binding job commitments with a consequence, not projections

strongest.why: A job ladder of 100 by 2028 rising to 500 by 2032 at 150 percent of the state average wage, secured by the state's right to raise the purchase price or take the land back.

local_contracting.label: Local contracting
local_contracting.asks: Local subcontracting goals and haul-route road repair paid by the operator

strongest.why: A separate county road-use agreement covering back payment, repaving two rural roads, and a performance bond for two more.

transparency.label: Transparency
transparency.asks: No NDA, the agreement is public, and an independent audit on a schedule

strongest.why: No NDA anywhere in the record, the whole file public, and compliance verified by outside professionals rather than self-certified.

tax.label: Tax incentives
tax.asks: A but-for test before any abatement, with the forgone revenue stated

strongest.why: No abatement at all. Full real property tax plus $4.15 per $100 on computer equipment, which funds roughly $1.3 billion of a $2.9 billion budget, banked against a stabilization fund.

strongest_note: The strongest version of each term that someone has actually signed, or the closest thing to it. These are judgment calls about real documents, not invented language, and they change by pull request like everything else here.
